headline: Google cuts Gemini 3.7 Flash API prices by 50% for coding and agents
summary: Google's latest AI model, Gemini 3.7 Flash, is now available with a temporary 50% API price reduction, aiming to boost adoption for coding and agentic workflows.
details: Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, an updated version of its AI model focused on coding, agentic workflows, and knowledge work. This release follows an unusually short three-week cycle since Gemini 3.6 Flash, driven by developer feedback and algorithmic enhancements.

For enterprise developers, the key attraction is the combination of improved intelligence with reduced inference costs. Through the end of 2026, Gemini 3.7 Flash is priced at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens. This introductory pricing offers a significant window for teams to evaluate potential reductions in operating costs.

The company is rapidly iterating on its Flash line, with the next flagship Pro model still pending release. Google has not provided a launch date for Gemini 3.5 Pro, despite it being in partner testing.

Google describes Gemini 3.7 Flash as its "most intelligent workhorse model yet for coding and agents." It's designed to adapt better to roadblocks, clarify intent, and follow instructions with greater fidelity, aiming for more disciplined execution with fewer retries and less manual supervision.

This evolution shifts the focus from simply minimizing agent steps, as seen in 3.6 Flash, towards investing more effort in planning and improving the quality of execution. Google DeepMind reports gains in debugging, issue resolution, and generating functional web layouts and applications with fewer prompts.

Google's own benchmarks show significant improvements in software engineering tests. On FrontierCode 1.1 Main, Gemini 3.7 Flash scores 43.6%, up from 34.4% for its predecessor, narrowly surpassing Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra. On DeepSWE v1.1, it reaches 65.3%, compared to 49.0% for 3.6 Flash, though GPT-5.6 Terra leads at 69.6%.

In web development, Gemini 3.7 Flash achieves an Elo score of 1588 on Code Arena, an improvement over 3.6 Flash and competitive with other leading models. It demonstrates enhanced ability to produce functional layouts and feature-complete applications with fewer prompts.

However, broader benchmarks show a more mixed performance. On Terminal-bench 2.1, Gemini 3.7 Flash scores 85.8%, slightly below GPT-5.6 Terra's 87.4%. GPT-5.6 Terra also leads on other terminal benchmarks, and Claude Sonnet 5 outperforms Gemini 3.7 Flash on Agent's Last Exam multimodal tasks.

headline: OpenAI replaces CRO, taps Wiz president Dali Rajic
summary: The AI giant is continuing its executive shake-up, bringing in a new top sales executive as it reportedly aims for a "relentless focus" on business impact.
details: OpenAI has appointed Wiz president and chief operating officer Dali Rajic as its new Chief Revenue Officer, replacing Denise Dresser after nine months. This move is part of a broader executive reshuffling within the company.
The shake-up also includes the departures of COO Brad Lightcap and CEO of AGI deployment Fidji Simo. Greg Brockman, OpenAI co-founder and president, is taking on a larger management role.

Rajic's previous employer, Wiz, was recently acquired by Google for $32 billion, making it Google's largest-ever acquisition. Brockman stated Rajic will "turn what we’ve learned into repeatable execution" to make AI broadly useful.
OpenAI products reportedly reach over one billion weekly active users and two million businesses. However, executives have indicated that the company has not met all of its revenue goals.

The company has filed confidentially with the SEC for a potential IPO, a common move to round out executive ranks. OpenAI also recently purchased $7 billion worth of employee shares, potentially signaling a delay in its public offering.

CEO Sam Altman has emphasized a focus on enterprise deployment, scaling back on experimental projects deemed distracting. This strategic shift aims to ensure a "measurable business impact" from the company's AI advancements.
